text:
Mira: Just pushed Orchid-7B-v2 to canary and then promoted after smoke passed. After quantization (4-bit PTQ) we're seeing repeating phrases in outputs for prompts >300 tokens and p99 latency up ~12% on Dedicated pool :confused:
Samir: can you paste an example prompt + output? Also which quant backend (awq/ptq/fused)?
Mira: example below:
```
# prompt id: onboarding-2026-03-19-01
Prompt: "Summarize the following long thread and list action items... (≈450 tokens)"
Output (truncated): "...the action items are: 1. check X, 2. check X, 3. check X, 2. check X..."
```
Mira: using PTQ 4-bit -- autocalibrate=true, kernel=fused_attn_v2
Jon: repro steps? exact curl / sdk call?
Mira: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"orchid-7b-v2-4bit", "input":"<long prompt>", "max_tokens":512, "temperature":0.0}'
Leah: noted on the latency increase — we bumped batch size heuristic for 4-bit in runtime last week. Could be batching change + kernel fallback.
Eva: repeating token patterns smell like KV cache / kv-rewind bug or attention mask mismatch after quant. Would like a small reproducible seed.
Mira: attaching minimal repro prompt and sample trace (will add logs). For now memory/perf highlights: canary hosts show CPU steal spikes, one host hit 95% GPU mem during regen loop.
ops-bot: deploy event: promoted orchid-7b-v2-4bit to dedicated pool at 2026-03-19T08:12Z — triggered autoscale.
deploy-bot: Canary health check: 12/15 OK, 3 degraded (high p99). Rolling back is available via /deploys/rollback <id>.
Samir: next steps proposal: 1) rollback to orchid-7b-v2-8bit on Dedicated if SLA impacted, 2) run offline deterministic comparison between fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit on the same prompts, 3) run KV-cache validity tests, 4) check runtime kernel selection logs. Can anyone own 2+3?
Jon: I'll take 2 (offline perf + quality comparison). ETA 3 hours. Will produce a quick notebook with perplexity / repeat-rate metrics.
Eva: I'll take 3 (KV-cache & attention mask tests). Starting with unit tests + a reproducer that toggles cache-reuse. ETA 2 hours.
Leah: I'll pull runtime kernel selection logs and batch heuristic diffs, also look at autoscale decisions that could explain CPU steal.
Mira: tagging customer impact — two enterprise tenants reported delays but no errors. I can coordinate comms if we decide to rollback.
Samir: If Jon/Eva repro shows it's quant-induced (quality delta > 3% repeat-rate) we should revert 4-bit to canary and schedule a quant re-run with awareness of attention kernel.
Jon: quick note: I'll include BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and a simple repeat-rate metric (n-gram overlap over sliding window).
Eva: KV tests found a failing case when using cached_prefixes + attention_slice > 1024 — dump attached. Hypothesis: quant kernels change memory alignment causing occasional cache misindexing.
Mira: nice catch. Can we patch a guard to disable cache reuse for affected requests until we fix?
Leah: yes, we can add request-level flag to bypass KV cache in runtime. I'll ship a quick config to canary edge.
ops-bot: action assigned: Jon -> offline-quality (due 3109887743), Eva -> kv-repro (due 3109884343), Leah -> runtime-guard (due 3109880943).
Samir: timeline decision: if deploy degradation still present after guard in 1 hour, rollback to orchid-7b-v2-8bit on Dedicated.
Mira: I'll hold on comms and monitor. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Jon: uploading initial comparison notebook to /shared/eng-ml/onboard/orchid7b/comp-notebook.ipynb
Eva: attached repro trace snippet:
```
TRACE: decode_step=214 repeat_window=32 token="check" kv_index=214 expected_kv=213 actual_kv=216
WARN: attention_slice=128 alignment_offset=48
```
Leah: pushed runtime flag canary: runtime.kv_cache.bypass_on_misaligned=true (applies to dedicated canary hosts)
Mira: after bypass flag, p99 latency improved slightly and repeat occurrences reduced in canary. Monitoring for 30m.
Samir: great. We'll regroup after Jon/Eva artifacts. If quality regression is confirmed, open a postmortem template and include quant config + kernel selection logs.
Mira: noted. Closing loop once rollback/patch decision finalized.
